sections.name: HeroBrain (part 1)
sections.title: Creating the scene and placing region labels
sections.what: Loads the 3D brain only when WebGL is available and creates it. Taps set the chosen region and node. Each frame, the region labels move onto their hub points and are nudged apart so none overlap.
sections.why: Loading only when needed keeps the page light, and nudging keeps labels from covering each other.
sections.watch_out: Region labels are moved every frame, so adding many regions adds work each frame.

sections.name: HeroBrain (part 2)
sections.title: Node labels, cleanup and selection
sections.what: Moves node labels onto their points and hides any that clash. Cleans up when the component leaves the page, keeps the chosen region and node in step with the 3D scene, and lets a second tap on a region turn it off.
sections.why: A second tap returning to the whole brain gives a simple way out of a region.
sections.watch_out: Picking a region also clears any picked node, so a region tap always resets the node focus.

sections.name: HeroBrain (part 3)
sections.title: Labels and hint text
sections.what: Draws the region and node labels as buttons over the brain, with a hint line at the bottom and a message if WebGL is missing.
sections.why: Puts clickable text on top of the picture while keeping the 3D drawing separate.
sections.watch_out: Node labels start hidden and only become visible once the placement code shows them, so they can briefly be missing.

sections.name: Readout (part 1)
sections.title: Detail panel for one node
sections.what: When a visitor has picked one node, this panel shows its name, code, hemisphere, a line of description, up to ten connected nodes, and an Open link if the node has a page. A back arrow at the top returns to the region the node belongs to.
sections.why: Lets visitors inspect one item and jump to related items without leaving the brain view.
sections.watch_out: The back arrow sends an empty id to onNode, so the parent component must treat an empty id as no node selected.

sections.name: Readout: if
sections.title: Region list or side overview
sections.what: When a region is chosen, this shows every node in it with its code, behind a back arrow to the whole brain. When nothing is chosen, it shows the left and right sides, each with its regions as buttons and item counts.
sections.why: Provides the menu a visitor uses to explore the brain, one level at a time.
sections.watch_out: The side captions are fixed text, and any region whose side is not left gets the right-side caption.

summary: The knowledge map in the hero: a brain you can turn and tap, with region and node labels placed on it and a side panel that explains what you picked.
purpose: Lets visitors explore skills and work by region and by node, with plain text explanations.
why: Likely reason: the brain is 3D while the readable text is kept in page HTML beside it, so the text stays clear and never covers the picture. The side panel comment says explanations sit beside the brain, never on top.
how: 1. Checks for WebGL, and shows a message if it is missing. 2. Loads the 3D scene only when needed. 3. Turns taps into a chosen region or node. 4. Each frame, moves region and node labels to their points on the brain, nudging them apart and hiding any that clash. 5. The side panel shows either the two hemispheres, the nodes in one region, or one node with its links.
inputs: Brain data (nodes, links and regions), WebGL support, the reduced motion setting, the screen width for low power mode, and the visitor's taps.
outputs: A labelled brain, and a side panel with descriptions, linked nodes and an Open link where a node has a web address.
risks: Labels are moved every frame, so many labels add work each frame. Going back from a node sets the focus to an empty string instead of nothing. It works today but is easy to break. The fallback is only a message, with no list of the content.
debug: If no brain appears, check WebGL in the browser and the scene import path. If labels float off their points, check the screen positions reported by BrainScene. If the side panel is blank, check the links and ids in the brain data. If an Open link is wrong, check its web address in the data.
